title: 2014 HMMT November Guts Problem 19
statement: Let a sequence \(\left\{a_{n}\right\}_{n=0}^{\infty}\) be defined by \(a_{0}=\sqrt{2}, a_{1}=2\), and \(a_{n+1}=a_{n} a_{n-1}^{2}\) for \(n \geq 1\). The sequence of remainders when \(a_{0}, a_{1}, a_{2}, \cdots\) are divided by 2014 is eventually periodic with some minimal period \(p\) (meaning that \(a_{m}=a_{m+p}\) for all sufficiently large integers \(m\), and \(p\) is the smallest such positive integer). Find \(p\).

solutions.text: 12 Let \(a_{n}=2^{b_{n}}\), so notice \(b_{1}=1, b_{2}=2\), and \(b_{n+1}=b_{n}+2 b_{n-1}\) for \(n \geq 1\), so by inspection \(b_{n}=2^{n-1}\) for all \(n\); thus \(a_{n}=2^{2^{n-1}}\). 2014 \(=2 \cdot 19 \cdot 53\) so we just want to find the lcm of the eventual periods of \(2^{n} \bmod \operatorname{ord}_{19}(2)\) and \(\operatorname{ord}_{53}(2)\). These orders divide 18 and 52 respectively, and we can manually check \(\operatorname{ord}_{9}(2)=6\) and \(\operatorname{ord}_{13}(2)=12\). The lcm of these is 12 , so to show the answer is 12 , it suffices to show that \(13 \mid \operatorname{ord}_{53}(2)\). This is true since \(2^{4} \not \equiv 1(\bmod 53)\). So, the answer is 12 .
